narrative.overview:
The projected scoreboard is a physical object: a sun-faded red header plank and four pale weathered team planks hung by rope from a crossbeam between two lifeguard-tower posts, standing on a beach of sky, ocean teal and sand. Every score and every timer digit is a cream wooden number card hanging from two brass hooks. Nothing glows, nothing is glass. Depth comes from paint over wood, soft cast shadows, brass bolts and rope, and the weight of cards that fall and swing.

The board speaks the show deck's language. Lettering is the deck's Josefin Sans, the show name carries the deck's plum drop shade, and each team keeps the identity it has in the deck: its own outline color, its pale stripe color and its Candice team-name lettering, set on a striped badge beside its animal. The tower supplies the hardware; the deck supplies the type and the team identities.

The board is composed once at a fixed 1920x1080 stage and scaled uniformly to the screen, so the room always sees the same picture. Density is low and type is huge: numerals are the content, everything else is hardware that holds them up. Texture is generated, not photographed: an `feTurbulence` wood grain multiplied over the paint and the team badges, bare-wood flakes masked to plank edges, plank seams, sand grain over the beach and a sun-fade on the red header.

The operator's control window is the same world at desk scale: sand-paper ground, cream boxes, Josefin Sans for headings and the large score readouts, team adjectives in their team colors, and a plain system UI face for everything the operator reads under pressure. It borrows the palette and the display face, not the wood.
keyCharacteristics: Painted wood, rope and brass; no gradients-as-glow, no glass, no neon.
One bold geometric face (Josefin Sans 700) for everything the audience reads; Candice only for team names.
Each team carries its deck identity: outline color, stripe color, Candice name, animal art.
Fixed digit slots: a number never reflows, a card swaps in place.
Change is a physical event: cards fall off hooks, new cards drop on with weight and swing.
Fixed 16:9 stage scaled to fit and clipped to its frame, never reflowed.

rules.name: The Paint Not Light Rule
rules.body: Color is paint on a surface. It is laid flat over wood grain and shaded by soft cast shadows; it never glows, blooms or gradients toward neon. The only gradients are physical: sky to sea to sand, a sun-fade on the red sign, the curve of a cream card, and the painted stripes of a team badge.

rules.name: The Two Flag Colors Rule
rules.body: Red and yellow are the lifeguard's signal colors and carry board state: red marks the header, the leader's flag and the TIME! moment; yellow holds the numbers. Team colors identify teams and never signal state.

rules.name: The Deck Identity Rule
rules.body: A team's two colors belong to that team alone, and they always travel with its name and animal. Color is never the only thing that tells two teams apart.

rules.name: The Back Row Rule
rules.body: If the audience reads it, it is set in Josefin Sans 700, except team names. System sans never appears on the projector.

rules.name: The Team Signature Rule
rules.body: Candice is only ever a team's two-word name. Each subset holds only that name's glyphs, so any other text in Candice will fail to render.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every numeral that can change uses tabular figures in a fixed-width slot, so a 1 never shifts its neighbors.

rules.name: The Gravity Rule
rules.body: Every shadow falls down and warm. Nothing floats on a neutral gray blur.

rules.name: The Sign-Painter Shade Rule
rules.body: A hard offset shade belongs only to painted lettering on a painted sign, in plum (the show name) or the sign's own deep tone. It never sits under a box, card or button.

dos: **Do** put every changing number on a cream card in a fixed hooked slot, with tabular Josefin Sans numerals.
**Do** make changes physical: fall, drop with weight, swing to rest, then a single chalk afterglow.
**Do** build surfaces as paint over generated wood grain, with bare wood showing only at plank edges.
**Do** hang things: rope, hooks, bolts and wires explain why every object is where it is.
**Do** give each team its deck identity together: outline color, stripe color, Candice name and animal art.
**Do** keep red and yellow for board state, and team colors for team identity.
**Do** honor `prefers-reduced-motion`: all animation and transition off, the placard simply present at time's up.
**Do** keep the control view in the palette and Josefin Sans, with system UI text for operator reading.
donts: **Don't** use glossy game-show panels, glowing gradients, glass or neon.
**Don't** let a number reflow its neighbors or change width as it updates.
**Don't** set audience-facing text in the system sans.
**Don't** put hard offset shadows under boxes, cards or buttons; that shade belongs to painted lettering only.
**Don't** set anything but a team's own two-word name in Candice; each subset holds only that name's glyphs.
**Don't** use a team's colors for another team, for board state, or as the only way to tell teams apart.
